101.description: Switching protocols. Text frames are `ClientMsg` from the client and `ServerMsg` from the server; exec I/O uses binary frames `[u32 sub id, big-endian][bytes]`.

force.description: Disconnect only: detach even if the container is running.

setup_open.description: `POST /auth/setup` is still accepted (the setup window has not closed).

BuildForm.description:
Multipart body of `POST /envs/{env}/images/build`: send `context` or
`dockerfile`, not both.

context.description: A tar of the build context.

dockerfile.description: A lone Dockerfile, when there is no other context.

tag.description: Tag for the built image, e.g. `app:1.2`.

oneOf.description: Exec stdin as text, for clients that cannot send binary frames.

ClientMsg.description:
A text frame from the client. Exec stdin may also arrive as a binary
frame of `[u32 sub id, big-endian][bytes]`.

errors.description: `name: error` for each container it failed on.

ContainerSpec.description:
Everything the create/recreate form edits. `advanced` is a Docker API
`ContainerCreate` JSON object merged over the generated body.

state.description: created | running | paused | restarting | exited | removing | dead

volumes.description: Names of named volumes mounted by this container.

start.description: Start the container after creating it (default true).

url.description: The Docker URL of a local environment; agent environments take none.

CreatedEnv.description: A newly created environment; an agent one carries its enrollment once.

truncated.description: True when the listing hit the size/entry cap and is incomplete.

DockerEvent.description: One Docker event, reduced to what the UI needs to patch its caches.

name.description: The actor's `name` attribute when Docker sends one.

join_token.description: Shown once. Valid for 15 minutes and for one agent.

EnvView.description: An environment as listed: agent environments carry their agent's state.

ErrorBody.description: The JSON body of every error response.

request_id.description: Matches the `x-request-id` response header and the server log.

cmd.description: `None` auto-detects a shell (bash, falling back to sh).

removed.description: Image ids deleted and tags removed, as Docker reports them.

text.description:
One line without its trailing newline. With `timestamps`, Docker's
RFC 3339 timestamp and a space come first.

tail.description: Lines from the end to start with; `None` means the whole log.

host_port.description: None publishes on a random host port.

oneOf.description:
A payload for subscription `sub`: a `DockerEvent`, a `StatsSample`,
an array of `LogLine`s, or a task progress message.
The logs queue overflowed and `dropped` lines were skipped.

The subscription is over. `reason` is `closed`, `ended`, `eof`,
`exited` (with `exit_code`), `succeeded` or `failed` (with `task`).

A request failed; `sub` is null when the frame named no valid
subscription. `code` is an error code as in `ErrorBody`.
An environment went up or down.

ServerMsg.description:
A text frame from the server, as the builders below write it. Exec
output arrives as binary frames of `[u32 sub id, big-endian][bytes]`.
Documentation only: `tests/openapi.rs` checks each builder against it.

StatsSample.description:
One stats sample for a container, with CPU already turned into a
percentage of one core times the number of cores (as `docker stats`).

target.description: What the task works on, e.g. the image reference.

task_id.description: Subscribe to it with the websocket `task` topic or poll `GET /tasks/{id}`.
